questions.q: What is the SI unit of velocity?
questions.explain: Velocity is displacement divided by time. Displacement is in metres (m) and time in seconds (s), giving m/s.
questions.tip: Velocity = space ÷ time. Think: how much SPACE in how much TIME.

questions.q: A car travels 100 m north, then 100 m south. What is the total distance and displacement?
questions.explain: Distance is the total path length (200 m). Displacement is the straight-line change in position (100 N + 100 S = 0).
questions.tip: Distance = total path. Displacement = net change. Round trip = zero displacement!

questions.q: Which equation relates velocity, acceleration, and time?
questions.explain: v = u + at is the first equation of motion, relating final velocity (v), initial velocity (u), acceleration (a), and time (t).
questions.tip: First equation of motion. Remember: V-U-AT (like 'VAT' on goods).

questions.q: On a velocity-time graph, what does the slope represent?
questions.explain: The slope (gradient) of a v-t graph is Δv/Δt, which is the definition of acceleration.
questions.tip: Slope of v-t graph = acceleration. Area under v-t graph = displacement.

questions.q: A ball is dropped from rest. What is its velocity after 3 seconds? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explain: Using v = u + at, with u = 0, a = g = 10 m/s², t = 3s: v = 0 + 10 × 3 = 30 m/s.
questions.tip: Free fall: v = gt when starting from rest. Multiply g by time!

questions.q: The area under a velocity-time graph represents:
questions.explain: The area under a v-t graph gives the product of velocity × time, which equals displacement.
questions.tip: Area under v-t = displacement. Area under a-t = change in velocity.

questions.q: An object at rest will remain at rest unless acted upon by an external force. This is:
questions.explain: This is Newton's First Law, also called the Law of Inertia. It describes what happens when no net force acts on an object.
questions.tip: First Law = Inertia. Objects resist changes in their state of motion.

questions.q: What is the formula for Newton's Second Law?
questions.explain: Newton's Second Law states that force equals mass times acceleration: F = ma.
questions.tip: F = ma is the most important equation in mechanics. Force = mass × acceleration.

questions.q: A 5 kg box accelerates at 3 m/s². What is the net force?
questions.explain: F = ma = 5 × 3 = 15 N. The net force is 15 Newtons.
questions.tip: Just multiply mass × acceleration. 5 × 3 = 15 N.

questions.q: When you push a wall, the wall pushes back with equal force. This illustrates:
questions.explain: Newton's Third Law: every action has an equal and opposite reaction. Your push on the wall is the action; the wall's push on you is the reaction.
questions.tip: Third Law: action = reaction. Forces always come in equal and opposite PAIRS.

questions.q: Which type of friction acts on a body that is already moving?
questions.explain: Kinetic (sliding) friction acts on bodies in motion. Static friction acts on bodies at rest.
questions.tip: Static = at rest. Kinetic = in motion. Static friction ≥ kinetic friction.

questions.q: The normal force on a flat surface equals:
questions.explain: On a flat horizontal surface, the normal force equals the weight mg. On an inclined plane, it becomes mg cos θ.
questions.tip: Flat surface: N = mg. Inclined surface: N = mg cos θ.

questions.q: Inertia depends on:
questions.explain: Inertia is the resistance to change in motion. It depends solely on mass — more mass means more inertia.
questions.tip: More mass = more inertia = harder to start or stop moving.

questions.q: What is the value of acceleration due to gravity on Earth's surface?
questions.explain: The standard acceleration due to gravity on Earth's surface is approximately 9.8 m/s² (often rounded to 10 m/s²).
questions.tip: g ≈ 9.8 m/s² ≈ 10 m/s². Remember: things fall FASTER every second!

questions.q: If the distance between two masses is doubled, the gravitational force becomes:
questions.explain: Gravitational force is inversely proportional to r². Doubling r makes the force 1/2² = 1/4 of the original.
questions.tip: Inverse square law: double distance → quarter force. Triple → ninth.

questions.q: What is the gravitational acceleration on a planet with mass 2× Earth and radius 2× Earth? (Use g = GM/R²)
questions.tip: Plug in 2M and 2R: g' = G·2M / (2R)² = g/2.

questions.q: Weightlessness in orbit occurs because:
opts: There is no gravity in space
The spacecraft is in free fall
Gravity is very weak at that height
questions.explain: Astronauts feel weightless because both they and the spacecraft are in continuous free fall around Earth — not because gravity is absent.
questions.tip: Orbit = continuous free fall. Gravity is still ~90% at ISS height!

questions.q: Kepler's Third Law states that:
opts: Planets speed up near the sun
questions.explain: Kepler's Third Law: the square of the orbital period is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis. T² ∝ a³.
questions.tip: T² ∝ a³. Farther from sun → much longer year!

questions.q: Escape velocity from Earth is approximately:
questions.explain: Escape velocity from Earth's surface is approximately 11.2 km/s. This is the minimum speed needed to escape Earth's gravitational field without further propulsion.
questions.tip: Escape velocity ≈ 11.2 km/s. Orbital velocity ≈ 7.9 km/s. Don't confuse the two!

questions.q: Work is defined as:
questions.explain: Work done by a constant force is W = F × d × cos θ, where d is displacement and θ is the angle between force and displacement.
questions.tip: Work = Force × Displacement × cos(angle). No displacement = no work!

questions.q: A 2 kg ball moving at 5 m/s has kinetic energy of:
questions.tip: Half × mass × velocity squared. ½ × 2 × 25 = 25 J.

questions.q: A 3 kg object at 10 m height has potential energy of: (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.tip: PE = mass × g × height. 3 × 10 × 10 = 300 J.

questions.q: The law of conservation of energy states that:
opts: Energy can only be transformed, not created or destroyed
questions.explain: Energy cannot be created or destroyed — only converted from one form to another. The total energy of an isolated system remains constant.
questions.tip: Energy changes FORM but never disappears. KE ↔ PE ↔ Heat.

questions.q: The SI unit of power is:
questions.explain: Power is the rate of doing work. SI unit is the Watt (W), equal to 1 Joule per second.
questions.tip: Power = Work/Time. 1 Watt = 1 Joule/second.

questions.q: A machine does 600 J of work in 30 seconds. Its power is:
questions.tip: Divide work by time. 600 ÷ 30 = 20 Watts.

questions.q: Linear momentum is defined as:
questions.explain: Momentum p = mv, where m is mass and v is velocity. It is a vector quantity.
questions.tip: Momentum = mass × velocity. Heavier or faster = more momentum.

questions.q: A 1500 kg car moves at 20 m/s. What is its momentum?
questions.tip: Multiply mass × velocity. 1500 × 20 = 30,000 kg⋅m/s.

questions.q: Impulse equals:
questions.explain: Impulse-momentum theorem: J = FΔt = Δp (change in momentum).
questions.tip: Impulse = change in momentum. A larger force over shorter time = same impulse.

questions.q: In an isolated system, total momentum is:
questions.explain: Law of Conservation of Momentum: in the absence of external forces, the total momentum of a system remains constant.
questions.tip: No external force → total momentum stays the same before and after collision.

questions.q: In a perfectly inelastic collision:
opts: Both KE and momentum are conserved
questions.explain: In a perfectly inelastic collision, objects stick together. Momentum is conserved but kinetic energy is NOT (some converts to heat/deformation).
questions.tip: Inelastic = stick together. Momentum conserved, energy NOT conserved.

questions.q: Centripetal acceleration is directed:
questions.explain: Centripetal means 'center-seeking.' The acceleration always points towards the center of the circular path.
questions.tip: Centri-PETAL = center-seeking. Always towards the center!

questions.q: A car of mass 1000 kg takes a turn of radius 50 m at 10 m/s. The centripetal force is:
Angular velocity (ω) is related to time period (T) by:
questions.explain: ω = 2π/T, where T is the time period for one complete revolution.
questions.tip: ω = 2π/T. One full circle = 2π radians. Divide by time for angular speed.

questions.q: On a banked road, the maximum safe speed depends on:
questions.explain: Maximum safe speed on a banked road (without friction) depends on the radius of the curve and the banking angle: v = √(rg tan θ).
questions.tip: Banking angle and radius determine safe speed. Mass cancels out!

questions.q: For a satellite in circular orbit, the centripetal force is provided by:
questions.explain: Gravity provides the centripetal force for orbital motion: GMm/r² = mv²/r.
questions.tip: In orbit, GRAVITY is the centripetal force. No rockets needed!

questions.q: Coulomb's law describes the force between:
questions.explain: Coulomb's Law gives the electrostatic force between two point charges: F = kq₁q₂/r².
questions.tip: Coulomb's Law = electric version of gravity. Same inverse-square pattern!

questions.q: A wire carries 3 A of current. How much charge flows in 10 seconds?
questions.explain: Q = It = 3 × 10 = 30 Coulombs.
questions.tip: Charge = Current × Time. 3 A × 10 s = 30 C.

questions.q: Ohm's Law states that:
questions.explain: Ohm's Law: V = IR, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.
questions.tip: V = IR. Remember VIR (like a name). Voltage = Current × Resistance.

questions.q: In a series circuit, which quantity is the same through all components?
questions.explain: In a series circuit, the current is the same through all components. Voltage divides across them.
questions.tip: Series = same current everywhere. Parallel = same voltage everywhere.

questions.q: Resistors in parallel have:
questions.explain: In a parallel circuit, each resistor has the same voltage across it. The current divides.
questions.tip: Parallel: same voltage. Current splits. Series: same current. Voltage splits.

questions.q: Electric power is given by:
questions.explain: Electric power P = IV. Also P = I²R = V²/R from Ohm's Law.
questions.tip: P = IV. Power = Current × Voltage. Remember: PIV (power, current, voltage).

questions.q: Magnetic field lines outside a magnet go from:
questions.explain: Outside a magnet, field lines go from the North pole to the South pole. Inside the magnet, they complete the loop from S to N.
questions.tip: Outside: N to S. Inside: S to N. They form CLOSED loops.

questions.q: The force on a charged particle moving in a magnetic field is called:
questions.explain: The Lorentz force on a moving charge in a magnetic field is F = qvB sin θ, directed perpendicular to both v and B.
questions.tip: Lorentz force = magnetic force on moving charge. Perpendicular to BOTH v and B!

questions.q: Electromagnetic induction was discovered by:
questions.explain: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction — a changing magnetic flux induces an EMF in a conductor.
questions.tip: Faraday's Law: changing magnetic flux → induced EMF. The minus sign is Lenz's Law!

questions.q: Lenz's Law states that the induced current:
questions.explain: Lenz's Law: the direction of induced current is such that it OPPOSES the change in magnetic flux that produced it.
questions.tip: Induced current FIGHTS the change. Nature resists change. The minus sign in Faraday's Law = Lenz's Law.

questions.q: The magnetic field inside a long solenoid is:
questions.explain: Inside a long solenoid, the magnetic field is uniform and directed along the axis. B = μ₀nI.
questions.tip: Solenoid = uniform B inside. n = turns per unit length. B = μ₀nI.

questions.q: The law of reflection states that:
opts: Angle of incidence > angle of reflection
Angle of incidence = angle of reflection
Angle of incidence < angle of reflection
questions.explain: Law of Reflection: the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, and both lie in the same plane as the normal.
questions.tip: Incidence = Reflection. Always. And both are measured from the NORMAL, not the surface!

questions.q: Snell's Law relates:
questions.explain: Snell's Law: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂, where n is refractive index and θ is the angle from the normal.
questions.formula: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂
questions.tip: Snell's Law: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂. Light bends TOWARDS the normal when entering a denser medium.

questions.q: A convex lens is:
questions.explain: A convex lens (thicker at center) converges parallel rays of light to a focal point. It is a converging lens.
questions.tip: Convex = converging (thick middle). Concave = diverging (thin middle).

questions.q: Total internal reflection occurs when light travels from:
questions.explain: TIR occurs when light goes from a denser to a rarer medium and the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle.
questions.tip: TIR needs: denser → rarer medium AND angle > critical angle. This is how optical fibers work!

questions.q: The refractive index of glass is 1.5. What is the speed of light in glass? (c = 3×10⁸ m/s)
questions.tip: Speed in medium = c/n. Glass (n=1.5) → light travels at 2×10⁸ m/s.

questions.q: The wave equation is v = fλ. What does λ represent?
questions.explain: λ (lambda) is the wavelength — the distance between two consecutive crests or troughs.
questions.tip: v = fλ. Speed = frequency × wavelength. Lambda (λ) = wavelength.

questions.q: Sound waves are:
questions.explain: Sound waves are longitudinal waves — the particles vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
questions.tip: Sound = longitudinal (push-pull). Light = transverse (up-down). Sound needs a medium!

questions.q: A wave has frequency 500 Hz and wavelength 0.6 m. What is its speed?
questions.tip: Multiply frequency × wavelength. 500 × 0.6 = 300 m/s. That's the speed of sound!

questions.q: The Doppler effect causes:
questions.explain: The Doppler effect is the change in observed frequency when there is relative motion between the source and observer.
questions.tip: Approaching → higher frequency. Receding → lower frequency. Think of a passing ambulance siren!

questions.q: When two waves of slightly different frequencies superpose, they produce:
questions.explain: Beats are produced by the superposition of two waves of slightly different frequencies. Beat frequency = |f₁ - f₂|.
questions.tip: Beats = wobbling sound from two close frequencies. Beat frequency = difference in frequencies.

questions.q: Sound cannot travel through:
questions.explain: Sound needs a medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to travel. It cannot propagate through a vacuum.
questions.tip: No medium = no sound. Space is silent! Sound needs particles to vibrate.

questions.q: Einstein's mass-energy equivalence is:
questions.explain: E = mc²: energy equals mass times the speed of light squared. A small amount of mass contains enormous energy.
questions.tip: E = mc². c² is HUGE (9×10¹⁶), so even tiny mass = enormous energy!

questions.q: The photoelectric effect demonstrates the:
questions.explain: The photoelectric effect shows that light behaves as particles (photons). Each photon has energy E = hν.
questions.tip: Photoelectric effect = light as PARTICLES (photons). E = hν (energy = Planck's constant × frequency).

questions.q: de Broglie wavelength is given by:
questions.explain: de Broglie hypothesis: all matter has wave nature. λ = h/p = h/(mv), where h is Planck's constant.
questions.tip: Every moving particle has a wavelength! λ = h/mv. Heavier or faster → shorter wavelength.

questions.q: In Bohr's model, electrons orbit the nucleus in:
questions.explain: Bohr's model: electrons can only exist in specific discrete orbits with quantized angular momentum (L = nh/2π).
questions.tip: Bohr's key idea: electrons in FIXED orbits only. No in-between states. Energy is QUANTIZED!

questions.q: Alpha particle consists of:
questions.explain: An alpha particle is a helium-4 nucleus: 2 protons and 2 neutrons, with charge +2e.
questions.tip: Alpha = helium nucleus. 2 protons + 2 neutrons. Heaviest common radiation.

questions.q: Nuclear fusion occurs in:
questions.explain: Nuclear fusion — combining light nuclei into heavier ones — powers stars. The Sun fuses hydrogen into helium.
questions.tip: Fusion = joining light nuclei. Powers STARS. Fission = splitting heavy nuclei. Powers nuclear plants.

questions.q: The Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle states:
opts: We can know both position and momentum exactly
Position and momentum cannot both be known precisely simultaneously
questions.explain: Δx × Δp ≥ h/4π. The more precisely you know position, the less precisely you can know momentum, and vice versa.
questions.tip: Uncertainty Principle: measuring one property disturbs the other. It's a fundamental limit, not a measurement error!
